chapters.summary: Nahum 1 declares God's judgment on Nineveh while comforting Judah, revealing that the LORD is a jealous and avenging God, yet shows kindness to those who take refuge in him.
keyPoints: The LORD is a jealous and avenging God who pours out wrath on his enemies, yet shows kindness to those who take refuge in him.
Nineveh will be punished for its sin; like a raging fire that melts the mountains, no one can withstand the LORD's fury.
Though Judah has suffered oppression, God will surely deliver her, declaring that the power of her enemies will at last be cut off.
chapters.application: When we face injustice, let us remember that God is a righteous judge who will surely vindicate the wronged; at the same time, let us take refuge in his steadfast love and find peace amid our troubles.

chapters.summary: Nahum 2 depicts the devastating fall of the city of Nineveh, declaring that God's judgment on this sinful city will surely come.
keyPoints: The enemy lays siege to Nineveh - chariots race through the streets, the walls collapse, and the city is plundered clean.
God exposes Nineveh's shame, leaving its palace desolate and its people carried into captivity - a picture of the downfall of the proud.
This judgment is just, for Nineveh's sins are full to overflowing, and God brings about retribution through the nations.
chapters.application: Let us examine our hearts and turn away from pride and sin, for God will surely judge all unrighteousness. May we humble ourselves and repent, that we may receive his mercy and salvation.

chapters.summary: Nahum 3 declares that Nineveh, filled to the brim with sin, will fall under God's judgment, meeting a tragic end that no one mourns.
keyPoints: Nineveh is full of lies, plunder, and prostitution, and God will surely punish her for these sins.
God exposes Nineveh's shame, making her an object of scorn among the nations.
Nineveh's strongholds are like fig trees with first-ripe fruit - once shaken, they fall, and no one is there to help.
chapters.application: Let us turn away from pride and sin, humbly relying on God, for he will surely judge all unrighteousness - yet he also gives us the chance to repent.
